title: Product Management and Design of Future Products
content:
At the UX Strategy Conference in Amsterdam I talked about how to product manage and design future products and the role of user experience in this process.

Designing for about-to-launch products is well documented. But how do you go about designing and testing the viability and demand of far-out product ideas for in 5 to 10 years? How do you launch an MVP for a product which is only possible in 5 to 10 years?

The core problem

The further out a product concept sits on the time horizon, the less applicable standard design and validation methods become. You can't test usability for technology that doesn't exist. You can't do market sizing for markets that haven't formed. And yet, if you wait until the technology is ready, you've lost the strategic lead time to shape the product well.

A different kind of validation

The talk proposed an approach to future product development that separates desirability validation (can we understand the need?) from feasibility validation (can we build it?) — allowing teams to make meaningful progress on the former well before the latter is possible.

Techniques include:

  • Futures research and horizon scanning
  • Design fiction and speculative prototypes
  • Early community building around the problem space
  • Partnerships with research institutions

About the talk

Presented at the UX Strategy Conference, Amsterdam.

Speaker: Remko Vermeulen, VP & Head of Product
